1:4.t: "Your joy": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts read "our joy".

2:23.t: "Whoever acknowledges the Son has the Father also": the KJV prints these words in italics, as missing from some of its sources; they are well supported in early manuscripts.

3:1.t: Many early manuscripts add "And that is what we are!"

3:14.t: "Their brother": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts read only "Anyone who does not love".

3:16.t: "The love of God": the KJV's reading; "of God" is in italics in the KJV, supplied by the translators.

4:3.t: "That Jesus Christ has come in the flesh": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts read only "Jesus".

5:7.t: "In heaven: the Father, the Word and the Holy Spirit; and these three are one. And there are three that testify on earth": the KJV's reading. These words, called the Johannine Comma, are not found in any Greek manuscript before the 1400s and appear in no early Greek writer; they entered late Latin manuscripts and were printed in the Greek text that the KJV translators used. Nearly all modern Bibles omit them. The teaching of the Trinity does not depend on this verse.

5:13.t: "And that you may continue to believe in the name of the Son of God": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts do not have these words.

5:18.t: "Keeps himself safe": the KJV's reading; many early manuscripts read "keeps him safe", meaning that Christ, the One born of God, keeps the believer.

1:1.t: "The Word of life" (Greek logos tes zoes): compare John 1:1-4.

1:3.t: "Fellowship" (Greek koinonia): sharing in common, partnership, participation; see Acts 2:42.

1:9.t: "Confess" (Greek homologeo): to say the same thing, to agree with God about our sin.

2:1.t: "Advocate" (Greek parakletos): the same word Jesus uses of the Holy Spirit (John 14:16). Here it means one who pleads our case before the Father.

2:2.t: "Atoning sacrifice" (Greek hilasmos): the KJV's "propitiation". The word carries both the turning away of God's wrath (propitiation) and the cleansing of sin (expiation). See Romans 3:25.

4:10.t: "Atoning sacrifice" (Greek hilasmos): the KJV's "propitiation". The word carries both the turning away of God's wrath (propitiation) and the cleansing of sin (expiation). See Romans 3:25.

2:18.t: "Antichrist" (Greek antichristos): one who opposes Christ or sets himself up in Christ's place. John uses it of false teachers who deny that Jesus is the Christ come in the flesh (2:22, 4:3). The word appears in the Bible only in John's letters.

3:6.t: "Keeps on sinning ... continue to sin": the Greek present tense points to a settled pattern of sin. John has already said believers do sin and need forgiveness (1:8-2:1).

3:9.t: "Keeps on sinning ... continue to sin": the Greek present tense points to a settled pattern of sin. John has already said believers do sin and need forgiveness (1:8-2:1).

4:8.t: "God is love" (Greek ho theos agape estin): love is God's very nature, shown in the giving of His Son (4:9-10). Agape is not mainly a feeling but committed goodwill that seeks another's good. See Matthew 5:43-44.

4:16.t: "God is love" (Greek ho theos agape estin): love is God's very nature, shown in the giving of His Son (4:9-10). Agape is not mainly a feeling but committed goodwill that seeks another's good. See Matthew 5:43-44.

4:18.t: "Perfect love" (Greek teleia agape): love brought to completion.

5:16.t: "A sin that leads to death": John does not define it. Readers understand it as a deliberate, final rejection of Christ (compare Hebrews 6:4-6, 10:26), or as sin bringing physical death as discipline (compare 1 Corinthians 11:30).
